headline: You can keep your belongings safe and be on the land while you build. Until permits exist, store things in a storage unit in town. Once the house permit is issued, add a permitted, painted container and live in a registered trailer.
key_points: You can store belongings on the land in a shipping container if it has a County accessory-structure permit (ACCR), under Information Bulletin IB-0002 (Jan 1, 2026). The container must be at least 5 ft from lot lines and 10 ft from buildings, outside easements and the front setback, and no more than 10 ft tall. It cannot be stacked, have utilities, hold flammables or have anyone inside. On Rural Living (RL) and Agriculture (AG) lots it must be painted or altered to blend in, and it must sit behind the house, out of view from the street.

You can place the container before the house is finished, but the County then also requires a Temporary Use Permit (TUP), plus a removal bond if the house isn't finished within 2 years. The house's temporary permit may be able to cover it as construction storage instead (ask County Land Use Services (LUS)). Inside the Town of Yucca Valley, one container is allowed on Rural Living lots of 2.5 acres or more (ask Town Planning about foundation and design rules).

For the first Bhutan trip (late March to April 2027), keep your belongings in a storage unit in town, because the lot has no permits yet. Yucca Valley listings start at $84 and $131 a month (sizes not listed). A 10x20 or climate-controlled unit costs more, up to about $250 a month (estimate).

A used 20-ft container costs from $1,800 at the BOXHUB Los Angeles depot. A used 40-ft starts at $2,200, a new 20-ft at $2,700 and a new 40-ft at $4,500. Standard delivery takes 5 business days. Delivery to Yucca Valley isn't priced, so plan on $500-1,500 (estimate).

Desert heat and pack rats are the biggest threats to stored things. An unshaded steel box in 100°F sun likely reaches 130-150°F inside (estimate). Shade the container or give it a white coating, set it on a cleared gravel pad, and use sealed totes and traps. Keep electronics, batteries, photos, art, wine, medicines and wooden instruments in climate-controlled storage in town.

You can safely reopen any closed space by following the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) hantavirus steps. Air out sheds for 30 minutes and vehicles for 20. Spray droppings with 1 part bleach to 9 parts water (about 1.5 cups per gallon) and let it soak 5 minutes. Wipe it up wearing gloves, and never sweep or vacuum.

Before any permit, County owners of 5 or more acres in Rural Living, Agriculture or Resource Conservation (RC) zones can camp on site up to 4 days in any 30. That works for weekend work trips, not for moving in. The Town has no camping allowance.

You can live on the land while you build, in a Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)-registered RV or travel trailer once the house permit is issued. The trailer also gives the site a daily presence. An imported capsule never qualifies as that interim home in the County or the Town. A park model may not either (ask County LUS before buying).

A capsule can be a storage room or daytime studio now. It can become a legal home only with a California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) insignia, applied at the factory after state plan approval, or a U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) label. None of the capsule sellers checked shows either one, so ask each seller in writing. Listings of about $19,000-24,000 become at least $25,000-37,000 after 28-53% import duties, and likely $35,000-65,000 once placed with freight, crane, foundation and hookups (estimates).

You can have the Sheriff act on trespassers while you're away. Under Senate Bill 602 (SB 602, 2023), a notarized owner's request can cover up to 12 months of absence, and the agency may accept it electronically on its own form. The Morongo Basin Sheriff's Station in Joshua Tree (760-366-4175) covers both the Town and unincorporated areas. Desert non-emergency dispatch is 760-956-5001.

A caretaker may be able to live on site while the build has an active permit. The County's 'Temporary Security Quarters' category allows a single-section unit for construction security staff, and the Town has a similar rule. It's unconfirmed whether a friend or house-sitter counts as security staff (ask County Building and Safety in writing).

You can get insurance even if regular insurers decline. The California Fair Access to Insurance Requirements (FAIR) Plan, sold through a registered broker, covers fire, lightning, internal explosion and smoke. Vandalism and malicious mischief coverage costs extra. Regular policies often limit theft and vandalism coverage after a set number of vacant days, often said to be about 60 (ask your broker for the exact clause).

risks.risk: A neighbor complains about people sleeping in an unpermitted capsule. In the Town that means a 30-day order to vacate. In the County it means citations of $100, $200, then $500 within a year, plus 50% late penalties at 30 and 60 days, and no new permits until enforcement costs are paid. That stalls the house.
risks.mitigation: Sleep only in a registered trailer under the temporary permit, once the house permit is issued. Use any capsule only for storage or as a daytime studio.

risks.risk: A long trip in the middle of the build lets the permit clocks run out. That also ends the right to keep the trailer and container on the land.
risks.mitigation: Travel mid-build only right after a passed inspection, for less than about 5 months, with any extension approved in writing first. Renew the trailer permit before you leave, and give a local person authority to schedule inspections.

risks.risk: An imported capsule ends up costing about 2-3 times its listed price after duty, freight and crane. It may also arrive with wiring that isn't listed for US 120/240-volt, 60-hertz power, which an inspector won't approve.
risks.mitigation: Get a customs broker's written duty estimate and the seller's written specs before paying any deposit. Or buy a unit with a HUD label, an HCD insignia or a Recreation Vehicle Industry Association (RVIA) seal.

risks.risk: Theft, squatting or dumping while you're away.
risks.mitigation: File the SB 602 trespass request for up to 12 months. Put a lock box and a puck lock on the container, and arrange a weekly check by a person. Add cameras if there's cell signal, leave nothing valuable on site, and meet the nearest neighbors.

risks.risk: Heat and pack rats ruin stored belongings, and you risk hantavirus exposure when you reopen.
risks.mitigation: Shade the container or give it a white coating. Use sealed totes and traps on a cleared gravel pad. Keep sensitive items in climate-controlled storage in town, and follow the CDC airing and bleach steps.

risks.risk: Insurance gaps: vacancy clauses, structures you can't insure because they're unpermitted, and the FAIR Plan's short list of covered perils.
risks.mitigation: Tell your broker your travel dates. Buy a vacancy endorsement and vandalism coverage, and insure the trailer separately.

questions_for_couple: Is a used travel trailer an acceptable first home on the land? What do you each love about the capsule idea: the look, the price or the speed?
Should the capsule money go toward a certified unit that could later become a permitted accessory unit, or toward a cheap trailer plus a capsule used only for storage?
Which belongings matter enough to pay for climate-controlled storage in town, and what do you sell or give away before late March 2027?
Who could check on the land every week while you're away, and what would you pay or offer them?
How long do you each want trips during the build to be? Are you willing to keep them under about 5 months, starting right after a passed inspection?
How much do you want to spend on security, such as cameras, a gate and lighting, compared with simply leaving nothing valuable on site?
next_actions: @computer Look up the parcel's assessor parcel number (APN) on the San Bernardino County parcel map. Note whether it lies inside Town of Yucca Valley limits and what its zone is.

@phone Call County Land Use Services at 909-387-8311 and ask Building and Safety three questions. 1) Can a container count as construction storage under the house's temporary permit, or does it need a Temporary Use Permit and a removal bond, and how large is the bond? 2) Does a house-sitter qualify under 'Temporary Security Quarters'? 3) Does a DMV-registered park model qualify as temporary quarters? Ask for the answers by email and note the staff member's name.

@phone If the lot is inside the Town, call Town of Yucca Valley Planning at 760-369-6575. Ask for the current Temporary Use Permit fee, and whether a container on a Rural Living lot of 2.5 acres or more needs a foundation or design treatment.

@email Ask each capsule seller to answer in writing: HCD insignia, HUD label or RVIA seal (yes or no); a US safety listing for 120/240-volt, 60-hertz wiring; the wind and tie-down rating; insulation R-values; and the Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) code.
@email Ask a licensed customs broker for a written duty estimate on one prefab building, HTS 9406.90.01.30, made in China, $20,000 free on board (FOB), entering through Long Beach.
@phone Call two FAIR Plan-registered insurance brokers. Get quotes for vacant-land liability, owner-builder builder's risk and trailer insurance, and ask for the exact vacancy clause in days.
@phone Call the Morongo Basin Sheriff's Station at 760-366-4175. Ask for the SB 602 trespass request form and whether Citizen Patrol does vacation checks.
@phone Get delivered quotes for a used 20-ft container from BOXHUB Los Angeles and one local dealer. Give each the road surface and the length of the approach.
@together Sort your belongings into three lists: on-site container, climate-controlled storage in town, and sell or give away.
@computer Reserve a climate-controlled storage unit in Yucca Valley by early March 2027, ready for the late March to April 2027 Bhutan trip.
